transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, what made me come in is that... the things that usually make me feel like myself have just started feeling really flat and heavy. I usually like going on photography walks, mentoring the kids, or even just keeping a really clean calendar—I'm an executive secretary, so staying organized is normally second nature to me. But lately, I just stopped initiating any of it. It all just feels like too much effort, I guess, and I wanted to talk to someone because it's just not like me.
About how long have you been feeling this way?

It's been... about a year and three months now. Yeah, right around then. It started after a family member of mine had some changes in their health and, um, their behavior. I ended up having to take on a lot more of the coordination for them, and I guess that's when things just started feeling like this.
Before this started about a year and three months ago, had you ever experienced a time when you felt this down or lost interest in things?

No, I haven't. I mean... sure, I've had bad days or stressful weeks at work before, but never anything like this. I've always been pretty driven and engaged with my life. So feeling this down and disconnected for this long... it's completely new to me.
How has your sleep been during this time?

My sleep has been a bit strange, actually. Um, there have been nights when I only sleep for maybe two or three hours. I'll wake up way before dawn, and instead of feeling tired, I just feel completely ready to go. I'll get up and start answering emails or updating appointment lists for work because I just don't feel like I need to go back to sleep.
When you have those times where you need very little sleep and feel ready to go, how many days in a row does that usually last?

Well, when it happens, it usually goes on for a few days at a time... maybe three or four days in a row? Like I said, I'll just get those two or three hours of sleep, wake up way before the sun's up, and I just feel completely energized. I don't feel tired at all, so I just start tackling my emails or organizing those appointment lists. It just stays like that for a few days before my sleep goes back to normal.
During those few days when you felt so energized and needed less sleep, did your mood also feel unusually high, irritable, or different from your normal self?

Yes, I'd say my mood definitely feels different during those times. I have these stretches where I feel unusually upbeat, like everything is just clicking perfectly. But then, if something small happens—like someone moving a meeting on the calendar—I can get really sharp with people. It actually surprises me how quickly I get irritable over something so minor.
